options.title: Why Did Nobody Use NVIDIA's First Chip?
options.first_line: NVIDIA's first chip drew 3D with curves instead of triangles, and almost no game used it.
options.first_frame: The NV1 chip already turning on a dark stage, a smooth curved patch bending up out of its die while a grey triangle mesh flickers beside it.

options.title: NVIDIA's First Chip Bet on Curves. Why Did It Lose?
options.first_line: Every 3D game is built from triangles, but NVIDIA's first chip refused to draw them.
options.first_frame: A glowing triangle wireframe of a game ship shatters into pieces as the NV1 chip slides in and the ship re-forms from smooth curved sheets.

options.title: What Was Wrong With NVIDIA's First Chip?
options.first_line: In 1995, NVIDIA sold a graphics card that almost no game knew how to use.
options.first_frame: The green NV1 board drops onto a lit studio floor, its gamepad ports glowing, while an empty game shelf beside it stays dark.

why: It names NVIDIA and a card no game could use, a mystery you can picture with the dark game shelf, while A and B already give away the answer (curves instead of triangles) so you'd have to stay to learn what was wrong.
